raw_text:
Below is a 12‑week, phased training and nutrition plan designed for fat loss and improved glycaemic control for a 45-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes (on metformin, HbA1c 7.2). It assumes access to a full gym and no contraindications beyond T2D. Encourage her to monitor capillary glucose and symptoms, and coordinate with her physician if meds need adjustment as activity and weight change.

Key safety notes for type 2 diabetes
- Check blood glucose before sessions, and carry fast-acting carbs (glucose tabs/gel).
  - If <90 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L): have 15–20 g fast carbs, recheck in 15 min; delay training until >100 mg/dL.
  - If >250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) and feeling unwell or ketones present: postpone training and hydrate.
- Avoid injecting insulin (if later prescribed) into areas about to be heavily exercised.
- Hydration: 500 ml water 1 hour pre, sip during; more if hot/humid.
- Foot care: moisture‑wicking socks, well‑fitted shoes, inspect feet daily.
- Metformin timing: generally fine around exercise; take with meals to reduce GI upset.
- Progress gradually; watch for dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, chest pain, or neuropathy symptoms.

Global structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and insulin sensitivity. Build movement quality, consistency, and aerobic base.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload and conditioning. Increase intensity, add intervals and volume.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Fat‑loss emphasis. Maintain strength, increase energy expenditure with mixed modalities.
- Frequency: 5 training days/week (3 resistance, 2 cardio/conditioning), 2 active recovery days.
- Daily step goal: Start 7,500–9,000 steps/day; progress to 10,000–12,000 by Week 8+.
- Session BG check: pre- and post- for first 2–3 weeks to learn responses; thereafter as needed.

Nutrition overview (specific, diabetes‑appropriate)
- Energy: Start at mild deficit ≈ 20% below maintenance. If unknown, estimate TDEE and adjust via weekly weight and CGM/glucose trends.
  - Rough start point: 14 kcal per lb of body weight for maintenance; set deficit at 11–12 kcal/lb. Reassess every 2 weeks.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight/day to preserve lean mass and improve satiety and glycaemic control. Distribute across 3–4 meals.
- Carbohydrate: Moderate and strategically timed; 35–45% of total calories from low‑GI, high‑fiber sources. Emphasize carbs around workouts; lower at sedentary times.
- Fat: 30–35% of calories, prioritizing mono‑ and polyunsaturated fats; limit saturated fat to <10% calories.
- Fiber: 28–35 g/day from vegetables, legumes, berries, whole grains that are well‑tolerated.
- Glycaemic strategy: Choose low‑GI carbs; pair carbs with protein, fat, and fiber; avoid sugar‑sweetened beverages and refined grains; limit alcohol (max 1 drink/day, with food).
- Meal timing: 3 main meals + optional protein/fiber snack if needed. Aim consistent timing day to day. Pre‑ and post‑workout carb allocation below.
- Hydration and electrolytes: 2–2.5 L/day water; add sodium/potassium with longer/hot sessions if needed.

Macros example (adjust for body weight)
- Example 75 kg client at 12 kcal/lb (~1980 kcal): Protein 130–150 g (520–600 kcal), Carbs 180–220 g (720–880 kcal), Fat 60–75 g (540–675 kcal).
- Carb timing:
  - Pre‑workout (60–120 min): 25–40 g low‑ to moderate‑GI carbs + 20–30 g protein.
  - Post‑workout (within 2 hrs): 35–50 g carbs + 25–35 g protein; choose low‑GI whole foods.
- Non‑training evenings: keep carbs lower (e.g., 20–30 g) and prioritize vegetables, lean protein, healthy fats.

Food lists and swaps
- Proteins: skinless poultry, fish (esp. salmon, sardines), eggs, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, tofu/tempeh, lean beef, whey/plant protein.
- Carbs (low‑GI/high fiber): oats/steel‑cut oats, quinoa, barley, brown/wild rice (small portions), legumes (lentils, chickpeas, beans), sweet potato, berries, apples/pears, nonstarchy veg, 100% whole‑grain bread (thin‑sliced).
- Fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts/seeds, nut butters, olives.
- Nonstarchy veg: leafy greens, crucifers, peppers, tomatoes, cucumbers, mushrooms, zucchini, green beans, asparagus.
- Limit/avoid: juices, refined cereals, white bread/pasta, pastries, fried foods, high‑sugar snacks.

Supplement considerations (optional; confirm with physician)
- Vitamin D3 if deficient; omega‑3 (EPA/DHA 1–2 g/day) if fish intake low; creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day can aid strength with no adverse effect on glycaemia in most; magnesium if low.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; consistent schedule; dark, cool room.
- Stress: 5–10 min daily breathing or mindfulness; chronic stress elevates glucose.
- Alcohol: With food, 0–1 drink/day, avoid on heavy training days.
- Menstrual cycle: Track symptoms; adjust intensity if energy low.

Warm‑up template (10–12 min each session)
- 3–5 min light cardio (bike/rower), dynamic mobility (hips, thoracic spine, ankles, shoulders), 1–2 activation sets for first lifts.

Cool‑down (5–8 min)
- Easy cardio 3–5 min + stretches for worked muscle groups; nasal breathing to down‑regulate.

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–4 – Foundation, technique, aerobic base
Goal: Build consistency, improve insulin sensitivity, master movement, modest caloric deficit.

Week 1
- Resistance A (Lower + push emphasis)
  - Goblet squat 3x10
  - Romanian deadlift (DB) 3x10
  - Split squat (bodyweight to light DB) 3x8/side
  - Incline DB press 3x10
  - Cable row 3x12
  - Pallof press 3x12/side
  - Finisher: 8–10 min brisk incline walk (RPE 6)
- Resistance B (Upper + hinge emphasis)
  - Trap bar deadlift (light) 3x6
  - Seated cable row 3x12
  - DB bench press 3x10
  - Lat pulldown (neutral) 3x10–12
  - DB hip thrust 3x10
  - Side plank 3x30–40 sec/side
- Resistance C (Full‑body circuit; technique)
  - Circuit x3 rounds: Leg press 12, Push‑ups (elevated) 8–12, DB RDL 12, Assisted pull‑down 10, Step‑ups 10/leg, Farmer carry 30–40 m
  - Rest 60–90 sec between moves
- Cardio 1: 30–35 min brisk walk or bike at RPE 5–6 (60–70% HRmax)
- Cardio 2: 25 min bike/elliptical, include 6 x 30 sec pickups at RPE 7 with 90 sec easy
- Steps: 7,500–9,000/day

Week 2
- Keep same structure; add 1 set to first two compound lifts of each resistance day (e.g., Goblet squat 4x8–10; Trap bar 4x5–6).
- Cardio 1: 35–40 min steady.
- Cardio 2: 8 x 30 sec pickups.
- Steps: 8,500–10,000/day.

Week 3
- Progress load 2.5–5% if all reps met; swap in:
  - Front‑foot elevated split squat 3x8/side
  - Chest‑supported row 3x10
  - Hip thrust barbell 3x8–10
- Cardio 1: 40 min steady.
- Cardio 2: 6 x 45 sec pickups (RPE 7–8) with 90 sec easy.
- Add core: Dead bug 3x8/side.
- Steps: 9,000–10,500.

Week 4 (deload-ish technique week)
- Keep weights same as Week 3 or reduce volume by 15–20%.
- Cardio: two sessions 35–40 min RPE 5–6.
- Focus on perfect form, mobility, sleep.

Nutrition Weeks 1–4
- Calories: start at 11–12 kcal/lb; adjust −100 to −150 kcal if no scale change by Week 3.
- Carbs ~40% on training days, ~30–35% on rest days. Prioritize carbs pre/post workout.
- Sample day (approx. 1900–2000 kcal, 145 g P / 180 g C / 70 g F):
  - Breakfast: Omelet (2 eggs + 150 g egg whites) with spinach/mushrooms + 1 slice whole‑grain toast + berries.
  - Lunch: Grilled chicken salad: mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, ½ avocado, olive oil/lemon; side of quinoa ¾ cup cooked.
  - Snack (pre‑workout): Greek yogurt (170 g) + 1 small apple + cinnamon.
  - Dinner (post‑workout): Baked salmon 120–150 g, roasted broccoli/cauliflower, small sweet potato (~150 g).
  - Optional evening: Cottage cheese 150 g with walnuts (10 g) if hungry.
- Monitor: Pre‑ and 2‑hr post‑meal glucose for 2–3 representative days each week. Aim post‑meal rise <50–60 mg/dL and <180 mg/dL at 1–2 hr.

PHASE 2: Weeks 5–8 – Progressive overload, conditioning
Goal: Increase strength and work capacity; introduce intervals to enhance insulin sensitivity and fat loss.

Week 5
- Resistance A (Lower strength + push)
  - Back squat or Hack squat 4x6–8
  - Barbell RDL 4x6–8
  - Walking lunge 3x10/leg
  - DB incline press 4x8–10
  - Chest‑supported row 3x10
  - Copenhagen plank (knees) 2x20–30 sec/side
- Resistance B (Upper strength + hinge)
  - Trap bar deadlift 4x4–6
  - Pull‑ups/Assisted 4x6–8
  - DB flat press 4x8
  - One‑arm cable row 3x10/side
  - Hip thrust 4x8
  - Anti‑rotation press 3x10/side
- Resistance C (Hypertrophy circuit)
  - Giant set x3–4: Leg press 12, Seated row 12, DB shoulder press 10, Romanian deadlift 10, Cable face pull 12–15, Sled push 20–30 m; rest 90 sec between rounds
- Cardio 1: Interval bike/rower 8 x 60 sec at RPE 7–8, 90 sec easy.
- Cardio 2: 40–45 min steady (RPE 5–6).
- Steps: 9,500–11,000.

Week 6
- Progress 2.5–5% loads or add 1 rep per set.
- Cardio 1: 10 x 60 sec intervals.
- Cardio 2: 45 min steady + finish with 5 min brisk walk cooldown.
- Add calf raises 3x12–15; side glute work (cable abduction) 3x12.

Week 7
- Change emphasis to unilateral and pulldown variations to manage joints:
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x8/leg
  - Landmine deadlift 4x6–8
  - Lat pulldown 4x8–10
  - DB incline 3x10–12
  - DB row 3x10/side
  - Hip thrust 3x10 heavy + 1 back‑off AMRAP set at lighter load
- Cardio 1: 8 x 75 sec at RPE 8 with 90 sec easy.
- Cardio 2: 45–50 min steady.
- Steps: 10,000–12,000.

Week 8 (consolidate/deload)
- Reduce volume ~20% or keep weight and cut 1 set from each exercise.
- Cardio 1: 6 x 60 sec intervals.
- Cardio 2: 40 min steady.
- Mobility emphasis and technique.

Nutrition Weeks 5–8
- Reassess weight, circumference, and glucose logs.
  - If average weekly weight loss <0.3–0.5% body weight and glucose still elevated, reduce calories by 100–150/day, primarily from carbs on rest days.
- Carbs: 1.5–2.0 g/kg on training days; 1.0–1.3 g/kg on rest days.
- Pre‑interval sessions: Ensure 25–35 g carbs 60–90 min prior to minimize hypoglycaemia risk during higher intensity work.
- Post‑workout: 35–50 g carbs + 25–35 g protein; include potassium/magnesium‑rich foods (leafy greens, beans).
- Example training day (~1850 kcal for 75 kg): 150 g P, 170 g C, 60 g F.
  - Breakfast: Skyr 200 g + oats 40 g + chia 10 g + blueberries.
  - Lunch: Turkey lettuce‑wraps + lentil soup (1 cup).
  - Pre‑workout: Banana (small) + whey 25 g in water.
  - Post‑workout/dinner: Stir‑fry: tofu 150 g, mixed veg, ¾ cup cooked brown rice; sesame oil 1 tsp.
  - Snack: Apple slices + 1 tbsp peanut butter.

PHASE 3: Weeks 9–12 – Fat‑loss emphasis, metabolic conditioning, strength maintenance
Goal: Maintain strength, slightly increase weekly caloric deficit via activity, preserve muscle, maximize glycaemic control.

Week 9
- Resistance A (Strength maintenance, lower body)
  - Back squat or Hack squat 3x5 heavy (RPE 7–8)
  - Hip thrust 3x6–8
  - Reverse lunge 3x8/leg
  - Leg curl 3x10–12
  - Plank 3x45–60 sec
- Resistance B (Upper body)
  - Trap bar deadlift 3x4–5 moderate
  - Pull‑ups/Assisted 4x6–8
  - DB bench 3x8
  - Cable row 3x10
  - Face pulls 3x15
  - Side plank 3x30–45 sec/side
- Resistance C (Mixed metabolic circuit)
  - EMOM 20 min, alternate:
    - Minute 1: Sled push 20–30 m (challenging)
    - Minute 2: Kettlebell swings 12–15 (light‑moderate)
    - Minute 3: Assault bike 12–15 cals or RPE 8 for 40 sec
    - Minute 4: Walk recovery and mobility
- Cardio 1: 10 x 60 sec intervals (RPE 8) with 60–75 sec easy.
- Cardio 2: 50–55 min brisk walk/elliptical RPE 5–6.
- Steps: 10,500–12,500.

Week 10
- Slight load or rep progression (stay shy of failure).
- Cardio 1: 12 x 45 sec hard (RPE 8–9) / 75 sec easy.
- Cardio 2: 55–60 min steady.
- Add finisher on Resistance A/B: 8–10 min incline walk or row at RPE 6.

Week 11
- Circuit variation:
  - AMRAP 3 rounds in 18–20 min: Leg press 15, DB push press 10, TRX row 12, Step‑ups 12/leg, Battle rope 30 sec; rest as needed to keep form.
- Cardio 1: 8 x 90 sec at RPE 7–8 with 90 sec easy.
- Cardio 2: 50 min steady + 10 min cool‑down walk.
- Steps: 11,000–13,000.

Week 12 (taper and assess)
- Keep resistance loads, reduce sets by ~25% to freshen up.
- Cardio: One interval (6 x 60 sec), one 45‑min steady.
- Testing/assessment: Repeat key lifts at Week 9 loads, measure body weight, waist/hip, and review glucose trends and symptoms.

Nutrition Weeks 9–12
- If adherence high and fat loss has slowed, implement one of:
  - Continue steady deficit; or
  - Introduce 1 high‑fiber refeed day/week at maintenance carbs focused around training to support performance.
- Training days: Protein 1.8–2.0 g/kg; Carbs 1.5–1.8 g/kg; Fats 0.7–0.9 g/kg.
- Rest days: Protein same; Carbs 0.8–1.2 g/kg; Fats 0.8–1.0 g/kg.
- Evening meals: Emphasize nonstarchy veg + lean protein + healthy fats; keep starch portions small (or shift most carbs earlier in day if evening glucose runs high).
- Example (~1750–1850 kcal for 75 kg):
  - Breakfast: Protein veggie scramble + ½ cup steel‑cut oats with cinnamon.
  - Lunch: Tuna salad (olive oil, lemon) in whole‑grain pita (thin) + side salad.
  - Pre‑workout: Skyr 150 g + kiwi.
  - Post‑workout/dinner: Chicken thigh (skinless) 150 g, roasted Brussels sprouts, ½ cup cooked quinoa.
  - Snack: Protein shake in water or cottage cheese + cucumber.

Glucose monitoring and adjustments
- Track fasting glucose, pre/post‑meal glucose, pre/post exercise for first 2–3 weeks, then at least:
  - Fasting daily.
  - 2‑hr post largest‑carb meal 3x/week.
  - Before higher‑intensity sessions for safety.
- Targets (general): Fasting 80–130 mg/dL; 1–2 hr post‑meal <180 mg/dL. Share logs with her clinician.
- If repeated lows (<80 mg/dL) around workouts: move more carbs to pre‑workout or reduce metformin timing with physician guidance.
- If post‑meal spikes >180 mg/dL persist: reduce that meal’s carbs by 10–15 g, add 10–15 g protein/5 g fat, and take a 10–15 min post‑meal walk.

Weekly structure (applies across phases; adjust as shown)
- Mon: Resistance A
- Tue: Cardio 1 (intervals)
- Wed: Resistance B
- Thu: Active recovery: 30–40 min easy walk + mobility or yoga, light core
- Fri: Resistance C
- Sat: Cardio 2 (steady)
- Sun: Active recovery or rest + 30–60 min easy walk

Active recovery and mobility
- 2–3 short movement snacks/day (5–10 min walks), especially after meals.
- Mobility: 10 min on off days—hips, thoracic spine, ankles, shoulders.

Progress checks
- Body weight: 2–3x/week, same conditions; aim 0.3–0.7% body weight loss per week.
- Circumferences: waist, hip, thigh every 4 weeks.
- Strength: track main lifts and RPE.
- Subjective: energy, sleep, stress, menstrual status.

Contingencies
- Time‑crunched day: Do compound moves only (squat/hinge/press/row) 3x6–10, then 10–15 min brisk walk.
- Joint pain: Substitute machines (leg press, cable row) and reduce impact; swap intervals to bike/rower.
- Travel: Full‑body hotel circuit 3x/week (squats, push‑ups elevated, RDLs with DBs, rows, step‑ups, planks) + daily 30–40 min walk.

By adhering to the above training, nutrition, and monitoring framework, she should see improvements in body composition, aerobic fitness, and glycaemic control, with safety for type 2 diabetes prioritized throughout.
